opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $187M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares) and $18M of related employer taxes.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $67M of share-based pay and $11M of related employer taxes, plus $1M of acquisition-related expenses.

opex.name: Disposal, restructuring and other
opex.note: One-off disposal and restructuring costs — excluded from Arm's non-GAAP results.

follow100Note: License revenue alone is $54.97 of every $100 Arm takes in. Tax took $11.28 of every $100 this quarter — a charge, after a $66M tax benefit a year ago. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Arm calls its direct cost 'cost of sales' ($32M). Tax was a $168M charge this quarter — about 35% of pre-tax income, versus a $66M benefit a year ago.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: up 45% YoY, vs $0.20 a year ago

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: non-GAAP, down 7% YoY; operating cash flow was $260M

oneTimers: Share-based pay is the main gap between the two profit numbers: the non-GAAP reconciliation adds back $261M of equity-settled share-based compensation (including $7M in cost of sales) plus $29M of related employer taxes (net of R&D incentives), $1M of acquisition-related expenses and $2M of restructuring costs, which is why GAAP net income of $313M sits far below non-GAAP net income of $641M.
Net income got a $20M lift from income on equity investments — a swing from a $290M loss a year ago. That is market-driven, not operating profit, and Arm excludes it from its non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Combined other income was $43M: interest income of $28M less a $5M other non-operating loss (together the $23M shown as other income), plus $20M of income from equity investments. Tax was a $168M charge, a 34.9% effective rate on $481M of pre-tax income, versus a $66M benefit a year ago.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 29% YoY on strong demand, the timing and size of high-value license agreements, and contributions from backlog.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 11% YoY on higher royalty rates from newer designs such as Armv9 and Arm CSS, with data center royalties more than doubling.

sources.label: Official earnings release — shareholder letter, Form 6-K Exhibit 99.2 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: License revenue rose 29% to a record $819M and royalty revenue 11% to $671M — also a record for a fourth quarter. Data center royalties more than doubled as Arm-based server chips spread, and Arm's share of CPU compute at the top hyperscalers is now about 50%.
takeaways.title: Both halves of the business set records

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.29 while non-GAAP EPS was $0.60. The gap is mostly $261M of share-based pay plus $29M of related employer taxes — and unlike a year ago, when equity investments lost $290M, this quarter they added $20M.
takeaways.title: GAAP profit is much smaller than the headline

takeaways.text: Customer demand for the Arm AGI CPU, Arm's first own data-center chip, now exceeds $2B across fiscal 2027–28 — more than double what Arm stated at launch, with Meta as lead partner. For Q1 FY27 Arm guided revenue to $1.26B (plus or minus $50M) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.40 (plus or minus $0.04).
takeaways.title: The AGI chip is the next growth bet

verdict: Arm closed fiscal 2026 with a record $1.49B quarter, up 20%, as licensing hit a record $819M — but GAAP profit of $313M was less than half the $641M non-GAAP figure, mostly because of $261M of share-based pay.
